share_verdict: A twentieth-century dish. We are not inventing it an ancestor.

source.text: Indian-Chinese restaurant practice, Calcutta and after

ingredients.name: cauliflower
ingredients.function: the substance. Cauliflower is a late arrival in Indian cooking, not a classical vegetable

ingredients.name: cornflour and refined flour
ingredients.function: the batter and the sauce thickener. Both are industrial-mill products

method_reconstructed: Toss in a soy, garlic and chilli sauce thickened with cornflour.
contested_points: This is a 20th-century Indian-Chinese dish. It has no ancient original and inventing one would be a fabrication.
Its usual origin story places it with Calcutta's Chinese community; specific attributions vary.

changed.driver: the dish is modern by design; only its components are open to substitution

ingredients: 1/2 cup chana flour (besan) and 1/4 cup rice flour, in place of refined flour and cornflour
1 tbsp rice flour slurry for the sauce, in place of cornflour
Cold-pressed groundnut or sesame oil for frying
Garlic, ginger, black pepper, a little jaggery, soy sauce
steps: Blanch the florets one minute so they do not need a long fry.
Batter in besan and rice flour, the besan browns better and adds protein and fibre the refined flour did not.
Shallow-fry rather than deep-fry, in a cold-pressed oil.
For the sauce, thicken with a rice flour slurry instead of cornflour. It sets softer and clearer.
Sweeten with a little jaggery instead of sugar.
Nobody should claim this makes the dish ancient. It makes it better on the fibre and protein axes, and that is the honest version of the claim.

verification.note: Classed MODERN_DISH. No ancient original is claimed and no locus is cited, so there is no citation to verify.
